newsitem.title: USA: Olympic Ethiopian runner held in woman's death.
newsitem.headline: Olympic Ethiopian runner held in woman's death.

text.p: An Olympic distance-runner from Ethiopia awaited arraignment in a Kentucky jail on Saturday in connection with the death a woman whom newspapers said was murdered for backing out of an arranged marriage.

FBI agents arrested Arega Gebrehiwet Abraha, 35, of Atlanta late on Friday aboard an airliner that had landed at the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport at Florence, Kentucky, an FBI news release said.
Abraha, who has lived in the United States since he was 16, was sought on a federal warrant of unlawful flight to avoid prosecution.

He was also named in an arrest warrant from the Dekalb County Superior Court in Atlanta, charging him with the Jan. 14 shooting death of Aster Haile, 28, his cousin. Haile's nude body was found alongside the Stone Mountain Freeway in Stone Mountain, Georgia.
News reports alleged Haile was killed after she refused to marry a suitor arranged for her by Abraha.
Abraha, an Olympic runner and winner of more than 170 distance races, was confined to the Boone County, Kentucky, Jail to face arraignment at a later date in federal court, the FBI release said.

Abraha had received considerable publicity for his efforts to promote world peace. He had met with President Bill Clinton, former President Jimmy Carter and House Speaker Newt Gingrich in that cause, according to Atlanta news reports.
